landing.title: Chronolignée
landing.subtitle: Explore your family through time.
landing.lead: A genealogy is not only a tree. It is lives that overlap, branches that migrate, sources that contradict each other — all of it in time.

time.title: Time as a dimension
time.body: Every life is an interval, not a date. The genealogical Gantt shows who was alive at the same time as whom.

evidence.title: Evidence before assertion
evidence.body: A birth date is not a field. It is a claim, backed by a source, and you can dispute it.

uncertainty.title: Uncertainty stays visible
uncertainty.body: "About 1877" never quietly becomes "1877". Soft edges stay soft.

landing.figureTitle: Thirteen lives of a fictional family, from 1779 to today
landing.figureDescription: Each horizontal line is one life, placed on a time axis running from 1770 to today. The vertical lines join a parent to their child at the child’s year of birth. Sharp ends are recorded dates, faded ends approximate or unknown ones.

duplicates.title: Duplicates
duplicates.lead: Two imports of one family leave the same person twice over. The search brings together records whose names resemble each other, then weighs the dates, the parents, the children and the places. It proposes: it never merges, and a father and his son of the same name remain two people.
duplicates.mergeIsForStewards: Merging retires a record from the tree: only stewards can do it. You can compare records and dismiss the matches that are wrong.
duplicates.searchInterrupted: The last search stopped short. Run it again.
duplicates.none: No match is waiting. The search compares names that are close, then the dates, the parents, the children and the places; it proposes nothing that a date or a family link rules out.
duplicates.comparisonLead: {percent}% match{signals}. The score only says what resembles what; the decision is yours.
duplicates.mergeKeepsEverything: Merging keeps everything: both dates of birth stay, one and the other, on the record that is kept. The merged record is not erased, it is withdrawn from the tree, and the history keeps a trace of the operation.
duplicates.mergeOnlyForStewards: Merging retires a record from the tree: only stewards can do it.
duplicates.confirmMerge: The record of <name>{of}</name> will be withdrawn from the tree. Its names, its events, its links and its sources move onto <name>{kept}</name>, which keeps its address.

ancestry.title: Ancestry
ancestry.lead: Sosa-Stradonitz numbering: the subject is 1, their father 2, their mother 3, and each generation doubles.
ancestry.tableCaption: Completeness of the ancestry, generation by generation

ancestry.deeper: The tree goes on beyond this depth.

descendants.title: Descendants
descendants.lead: d’Aboville numbering: the subject is 1, their children 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 in order of birth, and each generation adds a segment.

fan.title: Temporal fan
fan.lead: The ancestry as a fan, where each ring is a year and not a generation. A branch reaching further at every step is a branch of longer generations; two ancestors at the same radius were born in the same years.
fan.subjectHidden: This person is protected. Their fan is not shown: its centre would carry their year of birth.
fan.noBirth: The date of birth of {name} is not known. The fan measures everything from it: without that starting point it would only be a fan of generations in disguise.
fan.thickness: Thickness: the uncertainty on the birth. A thin line is a date; a wide band, “about” or “between”.
fan.pale: Pale: approximate or open date. Red: born after the person at the centre.
fan.unplacedLead: In the ancestry, but with no position in time. Placing them somewhere would invent exactly what the fan shows.

story.title: Follow the line back
story.lead: Generation after generation, into the past. Every sentence comes from a recorded fact and points to its sources; what is not in the tree is not in the story.
story.subjectHidden: This person is protected. Their story is not shown: it would begin with their own birth.
story.heading: Follow the line back — {name}
story.narrativeLanguage: The narrative itself is written in French: it is generated from the records, and its sentences are not translated yet.
story.suggestedLead: Stories the tree already contains: a long move, the line that reaches furthest back, a well-documented life, four generations alive at once. Each story is told from the data, with its sources; living people are never part of one.
story.notEnough: Not enough data for a story yet: it takes at least a line of three generations, a move between two located places, or a life with several sourced events.

statistics.title: Statistics
statistics.lead: What the recorded records say: when the family was born, how long it lived, at what age it married, what it was called.
statistics.headline: Main figures
statistics.caveat: These figures describe the recorded tree, not a population: a tree often follows one line more than the others, and children who died young are often missing from the registers. An age is computed only between two dates known to within a year; protected people are not counted.
statistics.century: {century, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}} c.
statistics.basedOn: {count, plural, =0 {no measurable data} one {from 1 person} other {from # people}}
statistics.couplesBasedOn: {count, plural, =0 {no complete couple} one {from 1 couple} other {from # couples}}

charts.ageAtDeath: Age at death, in ten-year bands
charts.lifespanByCentury: Median lifespan, by century of birth

figures.title: Ages
figures.lead: Medians: the middle value, which a lone centenarian does not move.
figures.marriageFemale: median age of women at first marriage
figures.marriageMale: median age of men at first marriage
figures.migration: Between the place of birth and the place of death, the median distance is {median} km ({count, plural, one {1 person} other {# people}}). The longest journey: {from} → {to}, {km} km.

atAge.title: At the same age
atAge.lead: The same birthday, one generation further up on each row: the year, whether they were alive, married, and how many children they already had.
atAge.nobody: At least one person with a recorded parent is needed.
atAge.caption: Comparison at {age}

viewer.keys: Wheel or plus and minus to zoom, arrows to move, 0 to fit, 1 for actual size, R to rotate, F for full screen.
viewer.failed: This document cannot be shown here. It can still be downloaded.

photos.title: Photographs
photos.lead: The family album. Everyone in it was recognised by someone who named them, never by a machine.
photos.noRecognition: No face recognition: people are identified by hand, and the versions shown carry no metadata (where the picture was taken included).

upload.formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or TIFF, 40 MB at most each
upload.privacy: The original is kept as it is for members; what is shown is a version without metadata.
